Serous acinar cell.description: Serous acinar cells secrete watery fluid rich in antimicrobial proteins like lysozyme and lactoferrin, found in nasal glands including Bowman's glands.

Mucous acinar cell.description: Mucous acinar cells produce mucins such as MUC5B to lubricate and protect the nasal cavity, located in submucosal glands.

Goblet cell.description: Goblet cells are mucus-secreting epithelial cells interspersed in the respiratory epithelium, marked by MUC5AC and TFF3.

Sustentacular cell.description: Sustentacular cells are supporting cells in the olfactory epithelium with detoxification and secretory roles, expressing cytochrome P450 enzymes.

Adventitial fibroblast (PI16+/CD34+).description: Adventitial fibroblasts surrounding blood vessels, marked by PI16, CD34, and extracellular matrix genes, playing roles in structural support and immune regulation.

Alveolar-like fibroblast (SFRP2+).description: Fibroblasts expressing SFRP2 and abundant collagen, responsible for maintenance of alveolar-like structures or soft tissue matrices.

Inflammatory fibroblast (CXCL12+).description: Pro-inflammatory fibroblasts secreting chemokines, cytokines, and matrix-degrading enzymes, driving immune cell recruitment and tissue remodeling.

Pericyte.description: Perivascular contractile cells that regulate capillary blood flow, often confused with fibroblasts but distinguished by RGS5 and PDGFRB.

Smooth muscle cell.description: Contractile cells of the vessel wall or airway, expressing smooth muscle actins and myosins at high levels.

Resident alveolar macrophage.description: Resident alveolar macrophages that maintain tissue homeostasis, characterized by high expression of lipid metabolism and efferocytosis genes.

Activated alveolar macrophage.description: Activated alveolar macrophages responding to inflammatory stimuli, producing cytokines, chemokines, and matrix-remodeling enzymes.

Dendritic cell.description: Conventional dendritic cells specializing in antigen presentation and T-cell activation, often confused with macrophages due to shared myeloid markers.

Naive B cell.description: Naive B cells expressing unswitched IgD/IgM, awaiting antigen encounter.

Memory B cell.description: Antigen-experienced B cells with class-switched immunoglobulins and rapid recall response.

Plasma cell.description: Antibody-secreting cells specialized for high-level immunoglobulin production.

T cell.description: T lymphocytes expressing T-cell receptor and co-stimulatory molecules, often confused with B cells in mixed clusters.

Monocyte.description: Myeloid cells with phagocytic and inflammatory functions, occasionally misannotated as B cells.

Nasal Superficial Goblet Cell.description: Goblet cells located in the surface epithelium of the nasal cavity, producing gel-forming mucins for mucosal defense.

Nasal Glandular Mucous Cell.description: Mucous cells within submucosal glands of the nasal mucosa, secreting mucins and antimicrobial proteins.

Club Cell.description: Non-ciliated secretory cells of the nasal epithelium, often confused with goblet cells due to shared secretory function but distinct ultrastructure and gene expression.

Ciliated Cell.description: Ciliated epithelial cells that may be misidentified as goblet cells in some single-cell analyses due to ambient or overlapping secretory transcripts.

Adventitial fibroblast.description: A subtype of fibroblasts located in the tunica adventitia of blood vessels, characterized by expression of CD34 and extracellular matrix genes, serving as a reservoir of mesenchymal progenitors.

Myofibroblast.description: Contractile fibroblasts expressing alpha-smooth muscle actin (ACTA2) and myosin, involved in tissue remodeling and wound healing.

Inflammatory fibroblast.description: Fibroblasts that produce pro-inflammatory cytokines and chemokines, recruiting immune cells and amplifying inflammation in the nasal mucosa.

Smooth muscle cell.description: Contractile cells of the smooth muscle, expressing ACTA2, MYH11, and DES, responsible for maintaining vascular and airway tone.

Pericyte.description: Perivascular cells that wrap around endothelial cells of capillaries and venules, expressing RGS5 and PDGFRB, regulating vascular stability and barrier function.

Solitary chemosensory cell (TRPM5+).description: Chemosensory brush cell expressing taste transduction machinery and cytokines, involved in sensing irritants and immune responses.

Microvillous cell (IP3R3+).description: Non-sensory microvillous cell of the olfactory epithelium with high IP3 receptor expression, likely supporting olfactory function.

Ciliated epithelial cell.description: Motile ciliated cell responsible for mucociliary clearance in the respiratory epithelium.

Secretory epithelial cell (goblet cell).description: Mucus-secreting cell producing mucins and antimicrobial proteins to maintain epithelial barrier function.

Mature CD1c+ dendritic cells.description: Activated dendritic cells expressing maturation markers and capable of migrating to lymph nodes to prime T cell responses.

Immature CD1c+ dendritic cells.description: Resting conventional type 2 dendritic cells with high antigen uptake capacity and expression of CLEC10A and FCER1A.

CD1c+CD14+ inflammatory dendritic cells.description: Monocyte-derived inflammatory dendritic cells co-expressing CD1c and monocyte markers, involved in innate immune responses and inflammation.

Langerhans cells.description: Epithelial-resident dendritic cells expressing langerin and CD1a, critical for skin and mucosal immune surveillance.

Plasmacytoid dendritic cells.description: Specialized dendritic cells producing large amounts of type I interferons upon viral stimulation, expressing CD123 and BDCA2.

Th2 CD4 T cell.description: CD4+ T helper 2 cells that promote allergic inflammation and IgE production, commonly enriched in nasal mucosa.

Regulatory T cell.description: CD4+ regulatory T cells that suppress immune responses to maintain tolerance and prevent excessive inflammation in the nasal mucosa.

CD4 tissue-resident memory T cell.description: CD4+ tissue-resident memory T cells that persist in nasal tissue, providing rapid localized recall responses.

CD8 T cell.description: CD8+ cytotoxic T cells that directly kill virus-infected cells and can be confused with CD4+ T cells due to similar activation profiles.

Innate lymphoid cell type 2.description: Group 2 innate lymphoid cells that produce type 2 cytokines and can be mistaken for Th2 cells due to shared markers like CRTH2 and GATA3.

CD8+ cytotoxic T cell.description: Effector CD8+ T cells with high cytotoxic potential, expressing granzymes, perforin, and transcription factors TBX21 and EOMES.

CD8+ resident memory T cell.description: Non-circulating tissue-resident CD8+ T cells expressing CD69, CD103, and transcription factor ZNF683, providing local immune surveillance.

CD8+ exhausted T cell.description: Dysfunctional CD8+ T cells with sustained expression of multiple inhibitory receptors such as PDCD1, HAVCR2, and LAG3, arising from chronic antigen stimulation.

Natural killer cell.description: Innate lymphoid cells with cytotoxic activity, expressing CD56 (NCAM1), CD16 (FCGR3A), and natural cytotoxicity receptors, lacking CD3/TCR.

Gamma-delta T cell.description: Unconventional T cells expressing gamma-delta TCR chains, possessing innate-like functions and rapid response to stress signals.

CD14++CD16- classical monocyte.description: CD14++CD16- classical monocytes are the predominant monocyte subset in blood, rapidly recruited to inflamed nasal tissues and characterized by high expression of pattern recognition receptors and pro-inflammatory cytokines.

CD14+CD16+ intermediate monocyte.description: CD14+CD16+ intermediate monocytes co-express CD14 and FCGR3A (CD16), displaying a mixed phenotype with enhanced antigen presentation capacity and often expanded in nasal inflammatory conditions.

CD14dimCD16++ non-classical monocyte.description: CD14dimCD16++ non-classical monocytes patrol the nasal microvasculature, expressing high levels of FCGR3A and CX3CR1, and are involved in surveillance and resolution of inflammation.

Monocyte-derived macrophage.description: Monocyte-derived macrophages differentiate from classical monocytes upon tissue entry, upregulating scavenger receptors (MARCO, MRC1) and lipid-associated genes, and adopt a pro-repair or pro-inflammatory phenotype in the nasal mucosa.

CD1c+ conventional dendritic cell.description: CD1c+ conventional dendritic cells (cDC2) are professional antigen-presenting cells in the nasal epithelium and lamina propria, characterized by expression of CD1C, CLEC10A, and FCER1A, and efficiently prime T cell responses.

Club cell.description: Non-ciliated secretory epithelial cells of the nasal respiratory epithelium that produce club cell secretory protein and participate in xenobiotic metabolism.

Goblet cell.description: Mucus-secreting cells that produce gel-forming mucins and other innate defense molecules to protect the nasal epithelium.

Ciliated cell.description: Motile ciliated epithelial cells that clear mucus and trapped particles from the nasal cavity through coordinated ciliary beating.

Sustentacular cell.description: Supporting cells of the olfactory epithelium that provide metabolic, structural, and xenobiotic-processing support for olfactory sensory neurons.

cDC1 (CD141+ dendritic cell).description: Conventional type 1 dendritic cells specialized in cross-presentation and antiviral responses, characterized by expression of CLEC9A and XCR1.

cDC2 (CD1c+ dendritic cell).description: Conventional type 2 dendritic cells involved in priming CD4+ T cell responses and promoting Th2/Th17 immunity, marked by CD1c and FCER1A.

Langerhans cell.description: Epithelial dendritic cells in mucosal and skin surfaces, identified by CD207 (langerin) and CD1a, involved in immune surveillance and tolerance.

Macrophage.description: Tissue-resident phagocytes that maintain homeostasis, clear debris, and modulate inflammation, expressing CD68 and CD163.

cDC1.description: Conventional type 1 dendritic cells specializing in cross-presentation to CD8+ T cells.

cDC2.description: Conventional type 2 dendritic cells that prime CD4+ T cell responses and promote Th2/Th17 immunity.

pDC.description: Plasmacytoid dendritic cells that rapidly produce large amounts of type I interferons upon viral sensing.

Macrophage.description: Tissue‑resident macrophages involved in phagocytosis, immune surveillance, and tissue homeostasis in the nasal mucosa.

Inflammatory macrophage (M1-like).description: Classically activated macrophages producing pro-inflammatory cytokines and chemokines, typically induced by IFN-gamma or LPS.

Pro-resolving macrophage (M2-like).description: Alternatively activated macrophages associated with tissue remodeling, anti-inflammatory responses, and phagocytosis of apoptotic cells.

Monocyte-derived transitional macrophage.description: Recently recruited monocyte-derived macrophages expressing both monocytic and macrophage markers, transitioning toward tissue residency.

Classical monocyte.description: Blood-derived monocytes infiltrating nasal tissue upon inflammation, often giving rise to elicited macrophages.

Conventional dendritic cell type 2 (cDC2.description: Migratory dendritic cells specialized in antigen presentation to CD4+ T cells, often found in nasal mucosa and draining lymph nodes.

Capillary lymphatic endothelial cell.description: Capillary (initial) lymphatic endothelial cells specialized for fluid and immune cell uptake.

Collecting lymphatic endothelial cell.description: Collecting lymphatic endothelial cells involved in lymph propulsion and vessel wall maturation.

Blood endothelial cell.description: Vascular endothelial cells forming blood vessels, distinct from lymphatic endothelium.

Pericyte.description: Mural cells wrapping endothelial cells, providing vascular stability and regulating blood flow.

Fibroblast.description: Connective tissue cells producing extracellular matrix and supporting tissue architecture.

Ciliated epithelial cell.description: Ciliated cells with motile cilia that move mucus and trapped particles, characterized by expression of FOXJ1 and various ciliary genes.

Goblet cell.description: Mucus-secreting cells producing mucins MUC5AC and MUC5B, essential for mucosal barrier function in the respiratory epithelium.

Club cell.description: Dome-shaped non-ciliated secretory cells with detoxification functions, marked by SCGB1A1 and CYP450 enzymes, and contributing to epithelial maintenance.

Basal cell.description: Stem/progenitor cells of the respiratory epithelium that adhere to the basement membrane and express KRT5 and TP63, responsible for regeneration.

Sustentacular cell.description: Supporting cells of the olfactory epithelium providing structural and metabolic support, distinct from respiratory epithelium by their expression of CYP2A13 and CPAMD8.

Mature Ionocyte.description: Fully differentiated nasal ionocyte expressing high levels of CFTR and other ion channels, responsible for transepithelial ion transport and fluid homeostasis.

Ionocyte Precursor.description: Progenitor-like cell co-expressing basal epithelial markers and early ionocyte transcription factors, representing a transitional state in ionocyte differentiation.

Tuft Cell.description: Chemosensory epithelial cell expressing taste transduction proteins, involved in detecting airway chemical stimuli and modulating immune responses.

Neuroendocrine Cell.description: Rare epithelial cell with neuroendocrine differentiation, secreting peptides and neurotransmitters to regulate airway function.

Nasal resident interstitial macrophage.description: Tissue-resident macrophages located in the nasal interstitium, involved in homeostatic clearance and immune regulation, characterized by high LYVE1 and FOLR2 expression.

Nasal luminal macrophage (MARCO+).description: Luminal macrophages in the nasal airway, analogous to alveolar macrophages, expressing high levels of MARCO and genes involved in lipid metabolism.

Inflammatory monocyte-derived macrophage.description: Recently recruited monocytes differentiating into pro-inflammatory macrophages, characterized by high expression of S100 family genes and pro-inflammatory cytokines.

M2-like macrophage.description: Anti-inflammatory, wound-healing macrophages prevalent in nasal mucosa, high expression of CD163 and MRC1, secreting IL-10 and TGFB1.

cDC2 dendritic cell.description: Conventional type 2 dendritic cells that prime T cells and often co-localize with macrophages in nasal tissues, distinguished by CD1C and FCER1A expression.

Mast cell T (MCT).description: Tryptase-only mast cells that are predominant in nasal mucosa and mediate allergic inflammation.

Mast cell TC (MCTC).description: Mast cells expressing both tryptase and chymase, located in nasal submucosa and involved in tissue remodeling.

Basophil.description: Circulating granulocytes that infiltrate nasal tissue during allergic reactions and are easily mistaken for mast cells due to shared markers.

Eosinophil.description: Granulocytes with eosinophilic granules that are recruited to nasal tissues in allergic responses and can be misannotated as mast cells.

Surface goblet cell.description: Mucus-secreting goblet cells lining the nasal surface epithelium, producing gel-forming mucins MUC5AC and MUC5B.

Gland mucous cell.description: Mucus-secreting cells residing in submucosal glands of the nasal epithelium, characterized by high MUC5B and MUC19 expression.

Gland serous cell.description: Serous secretory cells of the nasal submucosal glands, producing antimicrobial proteins like lactoferrin and lysozyme.

Ciliated epithelial cell.description: Motile ciliated cells that drive mucociliary clearance of the nasal epithelium.

Basal epithelial cell.description: Progenitor cell population of the airway epithelium, characterized by keratin 5 and p63 expression.

Mature Ciliated Cells.description: Fully differentiated multiciliated cells responsible for mucociliary clearance in the nasal respiratory epithelium.

Deuterosomal Cells.description: Multiciliated cell precursors undergoing deuterosome-mediated centriole amplification, characterized by cell cycle re-entry and early ciliogenesis genes.

Club-Ciliated Cells.description: Rare hybrid cells co-expressing secretory (club) cell markers and ciliated cell transcription factors, potentially representing a transitional state or distinct functional subset.

Basal Cell.description: Progenitor cells of the nasal respiratory epithelium, expressing KRT5 and TP63, sometimes misannotated as ciliated in low-quality droplets.

Secretory Cell (Goblet/Club).description: Secretory epithelial cells including goblet and club cells in nasal mucosa, expressing mucins and secretoglobins.

Ionocyte.description: Rare nasal epithelial cell type expressing CFTR and FOXI1, involved in ion transport, occasionally mistaken for ciliated cells due to mixed transcriptional signatures.

Tuft Cell.description: Chemosensory epithelial cells marked by POU2F3 and AVIL, part of the nasal innate immunity system.

Ciliated (Foxj1-driven).description: A subtype of multiciliated epithelial cell driven by FOXJ1, characterized by early ciliogenesis and axonemal dynein components.

Ciliated (Tppp3-rich).description: A subtype enriched in TPPP3 and radial spoke components, associated with mature motile cilia function.

Ciliated (Caps-rich).description: A subtype with high CAPS and cilia- and flagella-associated proteins, possibly specialized in mucociliary clearance regulation.

Secretory Club Cell.description: A non-ciliated secretory epithelial cell expressing club cell markers, often confused with multiciliated cells due to its apical location.

Goblet Cell.description: A mucin-producing cell type frequently neighboring multiciliated cells, distinguishable by its high expression of gel-forming mucins.

nasal surface goblet cell.description: Surface epithelial goblet cells in the nasal mucosa responsible for secreting the gel-forming mucin MUC5AC onto the airway surface.

nasal glandular mucous cell.description: Mucous cells within submucosal glands of the nasal mucosa that primarily produce the mucin MUC5B and contribute to the viscous gel layer.

nasal club cell.description: Non-ciliated, secretory epithelial cells of the distal airways/nasal passages that detoxify xenobiotics and secrete SCGB1A1, often acting as progenitor cells.

nasal serous cell.description: Protein-secreting cells of submucosal glands in the nose that produce abundant antimicrobial peptides and immunoglobulins into the airway liquid.

CD56bright NK cell.description: CD56bright NK cells are cytokine-producing immunoregulatory cells abundant in nasal mucosa, characterized by high NCAM1, SELL, and low FCGR3A.

CD56dim NK cell.description: CD56dim NK cells are mature cytotoxic effectors with high FCGR3A, PRF1, GZMB, and KIR expression, mediating direct target cell killing in nasal tissues.

Tissue-resident NK cell.description: Tissue-resident NK cells in the nasal mucosa are non-circulating, with ITGA1, ITGAE, CD69, and high responsiveness to local cytokines.

Innate lymphoid cell 1 (ILC1).description: ILC1s are innate lymphocytes resembling NK cells but with IL7R and KIT expression, producing IFN-γ in response to IL-12/IL-18 in nasal mucosal barriers.

Non-classical monocyte (CD16+).description: Patrolling non-classical monocytes with high CD16, CX3CR1, and interferon response gene expression.

Intermediate monocyte (CD14+ CD16+).description: Pro-inflammatory intermediate monocytes co-expressing CD14 and CD16, enriched for antigen presentation and cytokine secretion.

Classical monocyte (CD14+).description: Classical monocytes expressing high CD14, S100 alarmins, and granule proteins, primarily recruited via CCR2.

Alveolar macrophage.description: Tissue-resident alveolar macrophages with high lipid metabolism, scavenger receptors, and immunosuppressive markers.

Plasmacytoid dendritic cell.description: Plasmacytoid dendritic cells specialized in type I interferon production, marked by LILRA4, CLEC4C, and TCF4.

IgA plasma cell.description: Mucosal plasma cells producing IgA antibodies, characterized by high expression of IGHA1, IGHA2, and JCHAIN with enhanced protein secretion machinery.

IgG plasma cell.description: Plasma cells producing IgG antibodies, often associated with adaptive immune responses in inflammatory conditions, expressing IGHG1-4.

Plasmablast.description: Proliferative precursors to plasma cells, co-expressing B cell markers and cell cycle genes, capable of differentiating into antibody-secreting cells.

Immature plasmacytoid dendritic cell.description: Resting plasmacytoid dendritic cell characterized by high expression of regulatory factors and low interferon-stimulated gene activity, primarily involved in immune surveillance.

Activated plasmacytoid dendritic cell.description: Activated plasmacytoid dendritic cell producing high levels of type I interferons and pro-inflammatory cytokines upon pathogen sensing.

Conventional dendritic cell type 2.description: Myeloid conventional dendritic cell with potent antigen presentation capabilities, often confused with plasmacytoid dendritic cells due to overlapping markers.

Classical monocyte.description: Blood-derived monocyte that infiltrates nasal tissue and can express dendritic cell markers, leading to misannotation.

Naive B cell.description: B lymphocyte sharing some surface receptors with plasmacytoid dendritic cells, commonly misclassified due to expression of CD123 and lymphoid morphology.

Nasal arterial endothelial cell.description: Endothelial cells that line the arteries and arterioles in the nasal mucosa, characterized by arterial-specific gene expression (e.g., GJA5, HEY1) and roles in maintaining vascular barrier and regulating blood flow.

Nasal capillary endothelial cell.description: Endothelial cells of the nasal capillaries, specialized for efficient gas and solute exchange, marked by high expression of CA4, PLVAP, and transporters.

Nasal venous endothelial cell.description: Endothelial cells lining the veins and venules of the nasal vasculature, characterized by expression of NR2F2 and EPHB4, and involved in leukocyte trafficking and return of blood.

Pericyte.description: Perivascular contractile cells that envelop endothelial cells in the nasal microvasculature, providing structural support and regulating capillary diameter, identified by RGS5 and PDGFRB.

Vascular smooth muscle cell.description: Contractile cells located in the walls of larger nasal blood vessels, expressing smooth muscle-specific markers ACTA2 and MYH11, and responsible for vascular tone.

Proliferative Respiratory Basal Cell.description: Actively cycling basal stem cell of the respiratory epithelium characterized by high expression of cell cycle genes.

Quiescent Respiratory Basal Cell.description: Non-proliferating basal stem cell of the respiratory epithelium providing the progenitor pool for differentiation.

Olfactory Horizontal Basal Cell.description: Quiescent stem cell of the olfactory epithelium, morphologically and molecularly similar to respiratory basal cells but located in the olfactory niche and expressing distinctive adhesion and signaling molecules.

Olfactory Globose Basal Cell.description: Transiently amplifying neural progenitor cell of the olfactory epithelium giving rise to olfactory sensory neurons and sustentacular cells, marked by proneural transcription factors.

Hillock cell (basal-like).description: Hillock cells retaining expression of basal markers KRT5 and TP63 alongside canonical hillock keratins and early differentiation markers.

Hillock cell (differentiated).description: Mature hillock cells characterized by high expression of cornified envelope precursors and late differentiation keratins, representing a squamous-like barrier state.

Basal cell.description: Airway basal stem cells expressing canonical keratins and p63, capable of self-renewal and differentiation into secretory and ciliated lineages.

Club cell.description: Secretory club cells of the airway epithelium, producing antimicrobial peptides and detoxifying enzymes, with high level of SCGB1A1.

Nasal Serous Cell.description: Secretory cell of submucosal glands producing antimicrobial-rich serous fluid.

Goblet Cell.description: Mucus-producing cell of the surface epithelium secreting mucins to trap particles.

Club Cell.description: Secretory cell of the bronchiolar and nasal epithelium with detoxification and immune functions.

Nasal Mucous Cell.description: Mucous cell of submucosal glands producing thick mucus distinct from surface goblet cells.

CD4+ T cell.description: CD4+ helper T cells that coordinate immune responses through cytokine secretion and interaction with other immune cells.

CD8+ T cell.description: CD8+ cytotoxic T cells that directly kill infected or malignant cells through release of granzymes and perforin.

Regulatory T cell.description: FOXP3+ regulatory T cells that suppress immune responses and maintain self-tolerance.

Natural killer cell.description: Cytotoxic innate lymphoid cells that lack CD3 and recognize and kill abnormal cells.

Natural killer T cell.description: T cells expressing both T cell receptor and NK cell markers, recognizing lipid antigens presented by CD1d.

Nasal Goblet Cell.description: Secretory cells of the nasal surface epithelium producing mucus, characterized by high expression of mucin and goblet cell-specific factors.

Nasal Submucosal Gland Mucous Cell.description: Mucus-secreting cells located in the submucosal glands of the nasal cavity, expressing gland-specific antimicrobial and secretory proteins.

Club Cell.description: Non-ciliated secretory cells of the nasal epithelium involved in detoxification and immune defense, expressing secretoglobins.

Ciliated Cell.description: Multiciliated cells of the nasal epithelium responsible for mucociliary clearance, expressing motile cilia-related genes.

Basal Cell.description: Stem/progenitor cells of the nasal epithelium that self-renew and differentiate into secretory and ciliated cells, characterized by cytokeratins and p63 expression.

Nasal serous acinar cell.description: Serous acinar cells of the nasal submucosal glands that secrete a broad array of antimicrobial proteins, including lactoferrin, lysozyme, and PLUNC (BPIFA1).

Nasal club cell.description: Club cells (also called Clara cells) are non-mucous secretory cells of the nasal respiratory epithelium that express SCGB1A1 and metabolize xenobiotics via cytochrome P450 enzymes.

Nasal goblet cell.description: Goblet cells are mucus-producing cells in the nasal epithelium that secrete gel-forming mucins MUC5AC and MUC5B, and are regulated by SPDEF.

Nasal ionocyte.description: Pulmonary ionocytes are rare FOXI1+ cells in the nasal epithelium that highly express CFTR and regulate airway surface liquid via ion transport.

nasal airway smooth muscle cell.description: Smooth muscle cells of the nasal airway wall, responsible for regulating bronchomotor tone and airway caliber, expressing contractile proteins and regulatory channels characteristic of airway smooth muscle.

nasal vascular smooth muscle cell.description: Contractile smooth muscle cells surrounding blood vessels in the nasal mucosa, involved in regulating blood flow, nasal patency, and vascular tone, sharing core smooth muscle markers with subtle vascular-specific arteriovenous differentiation.

pericyte.description: Mural cells associated with capillaries and microvessels, regulating vascular permeability and angiogenesis, often confused with smooth muscle due to expression of some contractile genes but distinguishable by unique markers like RGS5 and CSPG4.

myofibroblast.description: Fibroblast-like cells with contractile properties, playing a role in wound healing and tissue remodeling, expressing both smooth muscle and extracellular matrix genes, frequently misannotated as smooth muscle in nasal tissues.

Conventional vein endothelial cell.description: Large-caliber vein endothelial cells expressing classical venous markers and high levels of von Willebrand factor, involved in blood return and hemostasis.

Post-capillary venule endothelial cell.description: Specialized venular endothelial cells expressing the Duffy antigen receptor (ACKR1) and high levels of adhesion molecules and chemokines, critical for leukocyte recruitment during inflammation.

High endothelial venule endothelial cell.description: Specialized post-capillary venules found in nasal-associated lymphoid tissue (NALT) that express mucosal addressin and chemokines to mediate lymphocyte homing.

Cavernous venous endothelial cell.description: Specialized endothelial cells lining the venous sinusoids of the nasal erectile tissue, equipped with vasodilatory and signaling machinery to regulate blood flow and congestion.

Arterial endothelial cell.description: Endothelial cells lining arteries and arterioles, characterized by high Notch pathway activity and expression of gap junction proteins, providing structural integrity and regulation of vascular tone.

Capillary endothelial cell.description: Thin-walled endothelial cells forming capillaries, optimized for gas and nutrient exchange, expressing high levels of carbonic anhydrase and nutrient transporters.

Lymphatic endothelial cell.description: Endothelial cells lining lymphatic vessels, expressing the master regulator PROX1 and involved in fluid drainage and immune cell trafficking.
